chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:
Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah and Salamah ibn Kuhayl entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him about a witness and an oath.
He said: "The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ruled by it, and 'Ali (peace be upon him) ruled by it among you in Kufa."
They said: "This is contrary to the Quran."
He said: "And where did you find it to be contrary to the Quran?"
Indeed, God the Exalted says: 'And call to witness two people of justice from you.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to them: "His saying 'And call to witness two people of justice from you' means that you do not accept the testimony of one person with an oath."
Then he said: "Indeed, 'Ali (peace be upon him) was sitting in the mosque of Kufa when 'Abdullah ibn Quf al-Taymi passed by him with the armor of Talhah.
'Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'This is the armor of Talhah, taken as spoil (ghulul) on the Day of Basra.'"
'Abdullah ibn Quf said to him: 'Appoint between me and you your judge whom you have accepted for the Muslims.' So he appointed between them Shurayh.
He said to him: 'This is the armor of Talhah, taken as spoil on the Day of Basra.'"
Shurayh said: 'Bring proof for what you say.'
So he brought him al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who testified: 'That it is the armor of Talhah, taken as spoil on the Day of Basra.'"
He said: 'This is one witness, and I do not rule by the testimony of one witness until there is another with him.'
So he called Qanbar, who testified that it was the armor of Talhah, taken as spoil on the Day of Basra.
Shurayh said: 'This is a slave, and I do not rule by the testimony of a slave.'
So 'Ali (peace be upon him) became angry and said: 'Take it, for this man has ruled with injustice three times.'
So Shurayh turned from his seat and said: 'I will not rule between two people until you tell me from where I ruled with injustice three times.'

He said to him: 'Woe to you! When I informed you that it was the armor of Talhah, taken as spoil on the Day of Basra, you said: Bring proof for what you say. And indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wherever spoil is found, it is taken without proof.'"
I said: 'You are a man who has not heard the hadith.' This is the first one.

Then I brought you al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who testified, and you said: 'This is one, and I do not rule by the testimony of one until there is another with him.' And indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ruled by the testimony of one and an oath.
So these are two.
Then I brought you Qanbar, who testified that it was the armor of Talhah, taken as spoil on the Day of Basra, and you said: 'This is a slave, and I do not rule by the testimony of a slave.'
And there is no harm with the testimony of a slave if he is just.'
Then he said: 'Woe to you! The Imam of the Muslims is more secure in their affairs than this.'

key_terms.غُلُولٌ: Spoil of war / booty taken before distribution
key_terms.يَوْمَ اَلْبَصْرَةِ: The Day of Basra (Battle of Camel)

ai.seo_question: What is the evidence for the validity of one witness and an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith elucidates the jurisprudential principle of *shahid wa yamin* (one witness plus an oath), a key distinction in Shia fiqh where the Prophet and Imam Ali accepted a single witness's testimony corroborated by an oath, contrasting with the general Quranic requirement for two witnesses. The narrative highlights Imam Ali’s critique of Judge Shurayh’s rigid application of Hanafi-style evidentiary rules, demonstrating that the Prophet’s precedent allowed for flexibility in identifying spoils of war (*ghulul*) and validating the testimony of slaves if they were just (*adl*). This serves as a foundational text for the Shia position that the Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt provides specific legal derivations that refine, rather than contradict, the Quranic text.
